newsitem.title: FRANCE: Possible to target French VAT cut - Socialist caucus.
newsitem.headline: Possible to target French VAT cut - Socialist caucus.

text.p: Jean-Marc Ayrault, head of the Socialist caucus in the French National Assembly, said on Tuesday a targeted cut in the country's Value Added Tax (VAT) may be possible even if an across-the-board reduction is not.

"An across the board cut (in the standard rate of 20.6 percent) is not necessarily possible but a targeted cut can be envisaged," he told reporters after meeting Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn.
He said discussion on the subject would be helped by completion of the government's audit of public finances, to be ready by July 21.

During the recent election campaign which brought the Socialists to power, the party talked of a cut in the "basic" value added tax levied on such goods as bread and milk to five percent from 5.5 percent.
Economists have calculated that such a move would cost five billion francs in lost tax revenue.

The previous conservative government increased the standard sales tax rate by two percentage points to 20.6 percent in 1995. The government said back then that the rise would be reversed once public deficits were brought under control.
